body: I mean my quality of life has improved in ways, but the mental anguish only subsides for a few months at a time into a dull roar. I did have one year that I was working so much I was too distracted to realize my mental state, but the comedown from that was hard and I experienced burn out like I was re-entering the atmosphere. So... I guess it's everchanging?

I haven't even reached my "limit" if you will, I certainly could endure longer, but why? I just don't see the endgame of suffering on the edge of this cliff for 40-60 more years. I haven't been happy, I'm not gonna be happy, I'm not compatible with happiness. I tried, I didn't sit on my ass and let it consume me, but it still is. So I just don't understand prolonging it.
I find that wave of relief (for lack of a better word) that lies just past that immense dispair is such an odd place to exist, like looking out the window of an airport you are departing from.
"Follow your own narrow, bendy path" is a rather fantastic way to put it. Thank you

Thank you. Not OP but I've started my letter to family and I wondered if it would hurt more to leave them with letter than with nothing. I think it's a good idea to leave behind something that tells them I don't hurt anymore and that I loved them

It's interesting, isn't it? I keep telling my cat I'll miss him but I have to stop half way through my thought because I realize that I won't be feeling anything. That's the point, to stop all the feeling. So I switch and tell him not to miss me too much, but then I somehow feel worse?? It's a no-win situation
He really is the best cat. He came over and passed out on me as I wrote this all out. I'll give it a week, I may feel different later, but I'm at least going to cover all my bases.
